question: Why does calling d.get('b', 'not found') not raise a KeyError even though 'b' is not a key in d?
options: Because get() ignores missing keys and returns None always
Because get() adds the missing key to the dictionary automatically
Because get() returns the provided default value instead of raising an exception when the key is absent
Because dictionaries silently allow any key to be accessed
explanation: dict.get(key, default) looks up the key and returns default instead of raising KeyError if the key isn't found, unlike square-bracket access.
